summary.headline: Softer week: orders down 6.1% to 696 and revenue down 9.1% to $49,640, both behind target, though still well ahead of last year.

points.what: Orders fell 6.1% week on week to 696 and revenue fell 9.1% to $49,640.
points.so_what: Both sit below the 8-week averages of 710 orders and $51,669 revenue.

points.what: Orders were up 44.4% and revenue up 37.3% versus the same week last year.
points.so_what: Both growth rates are below the 75% growth the 2026 targets assume.

points.what: The week reached 82.4% of the 845-order target and 83.0% of the $59,794 revenue target.
points.so_what: The week closed $10,154 short of its revenue target, leaving the quarter further behind.

points.what: The cancellation rate improved 1.3 pp to 14.8%, while the 14-Day Return Rate for the week of 26 Jan 2026 rose 2.2 pp to 11.6%.
points.so_what: Order quality signals point in opposite directions this week.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 26 Jan 2026 was 11.6%, up 2.2 pp, above the 1.0 pp notable threshold.
points.so_what: The two most recent weeks are not yet mature, so this is the latest complete read on returns.

points.what: The cancellation rate moved 1.3 pp to 14.8%, a notable change by the 1.0 pp threshold.
points.so_what: Each percentage point of cancellations is worth about $583 of weekly revenue.

points.what: QTD revenue is 87.4% of target at $361,944, a gap of $52,211 with 6 weeks left in the quarter.
points.so_what: Reaching the $774,555 full-quarter target requires $412,611 over those 6 weeks.

points.what: Weekly orders reached 82.4% of the 845-order target (gap of 149) and revenue 83.0% of the $59,794 target (gap of $10,154).
points.so_what: Next week's targets step to 802 orders and $59,585 of revenue.

points.what: QTD revenue of $361,944 is 87.4% of the $414,155 target to date, behind by $52,211.
points.so_what: Both Jan and Feb to date are behind target, at 88.0% and 86.0% attainment.

points.what: YTD revenue is 87.4% of target, and the full-year target of $3,888,802 needs $76,671 per week for the remaining 46 weeks.
points.so_what: That is well above the recent 8-week run-rate of $51,543 per week.

points.what: APAC orders fell 22 to 317 and LATAM fell 22 to 81, each accounting for 48.9% of the total order decline.
points.so_what: LATAM produced the same order loss as APAC from a base of 103, versus APAC's 339.

points.what: Organic orders fell 25.9% to 83, a contribution of -29 orders, or 64.4% of the week's change.
points.so_what: Organic alone accounts for more than the net decline of 45 orders.

points.what: Search, the largest source at 72.8% of orders, slipped 1.9% to 507, while Display rose 16.7% to 28.
points.so_what: Display's gain of 4 orders offsets only a small part of the losses elsewhere.

points.what: The cancellation rate improved 1.3 pp week on week to 14.8%, and was 0.6 pp below the same week last year.
points.so_what: At about $583 of weekly revenue per percentage point, this level of cancellations is worth watching against the revenue gap.

points.what: AOV fell 4.7% to $83.71 and was 5.5% below last year.
points.so_what: This explains why revenue fell 9.1% while orders fell only 6.1%.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 26 Jan 2026 was 11.6%, up 2.2 pp both week on week and year on year.
points.so_what: Returns are not deducted from gross revenue, so this does not reduce the reported revenue figure.

points.what: New signups were flat at 223, and down 3.9% year on year, while orders grew 44.4% year on year.
points.so_what: Order growth is running well ahead of customer acquisition growth.

summary.headline: Orders and revenue fell week on week and stayed behind target, though both remain well above last year; returns rose in the mature week.

points.what: Orders fell 6.1% to 696 and revenue fell 9.1% to $49,640, both rated bad week on week.
points.so_what: Both sit below the 8-week averages of 710 orders and $51,669 revenue.

points.what: Revenue reached 83.0% of the weekly target of $59,794, a gap of $10,154, and orders reached 82.4% of the 845 target.
points.so_what: Next week needs $59,585 of revenue and 802 orders to meet target.

points.what: Orders grew 44.4% and revenue 37.3% versus last year, both rated good.
points.so_what: Both remain below the 75% growth the 2026 targets assume.

points.what: The cancellation rate improved 1.3 pp to 14.8%, while the 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 26 Jan 2026 rose 2.2 pp to 11.6%.
points.so_what: Order quality moved in opposite directions on the two measures this week.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 26 Jan 2026 rose 2.2 pp to 11.6%, above the 1.0 pp notable threshold, and is also 2.2 pp above last year.
points.so_what: The two most recent weeks are not yet mature, so their return rates are not reported.

points.what: The cancellation rate fell 1.3 pp to 14.8%, a notable move rated good.
points.so_what: Each percentage point of cancellations is worth about $583 of revenue.

points.what: QTD revenue is $361,944 against a target to date of $414,155, 87.4% attainment and a gap of $52,211.
points.so_what: Reaching the full quarter target of $774,555 needs $412,611 in the remaining 6 weeks.

points.what: Weekly revenue was 83.0% of target ($49,640 vs $59,794) and weekly orders 82.4% of target (696 vs 845), both behind.
points.so_what: Next week's targets are $59,585 of revenue and 802 orders.

points.what: QTD revenue attainment is 87.4%, behind target by $52,211 with 6 weeks left in the quarter.
points.so_what: $412,611 is still required to reach the full quarter target of $774,555.

points.what: YTD revenue is $361,944, 87.4% of target, and the full-year target of $3,888,802 needs $76,671 a week versus the current 8-week run-rate of $51,543.
points.so_what: The required pace is well above the recent pace, and both Jan and Feb MTD are behind target.

points.what: APAC orders fell 22 to 317, and LATAM also fell 22 to 81, each accounting for 48.9% of the WoW decline.
points.so_what: These two regions explain nearly all of the 45-order decline, with LATAM's 21.4% drop the steepest.

points.what: Organic orders fell 29 to 83, the largest single contributor at 64.4% of the change, while Search fell 10 to 507.
points.so_what: Search still carries 72.8% of orders, so its 1.9% dip matters less in percent than in volume.

points.what: North America orders rose 1.8% to 169 and Display rose 16.7% to 28, the only segments up week on week.
points.so_what: These gains were too small to offset the declines elsewhere.

points.what: AOV fell 4.7% to $83.71 week on week and is down 5.5% versus last year, both rated bad.
points.so_what: Revenue fell faster than orders (-9.1% vs -6.1%) as a result of the lower value per order.

points.what: The cancellation rate improved 1.3 pp to 14.8%, and is 0.6 pp below last year.
points.so_what: At about $583 of revenue per percentage point, this is a modest positive for the week's revenue.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 26 Jan 2026 was 11.6%, up 2.2 pp on the prior week and 2.2 pp on last year.
points.so_what: This is customer return behavior for an earlier week, not the reporting week.

points.what: New signups were flat at 223 and down 3.9% versus last year, rated bad on the year.
points.so_what: Signups are not growing while orders are up 44.4% year on year.
